planting_details.assumptions_or_notes: Rainfed long-rains season; smallholder practice with 75 cm rows and ~25 cm within-row spacing (≈53,000 plants/ha). H614 is a high-altitude hybrid commonly grown in Trans-Nzoia. Planting depth 5 cm chosen for adequate soil moisture and seed size. Row direction unknown, set to -99.

events.Assumptions_or_Notes: Basal placement at planting using diammonium phosphate (DAP, 18-46-0). Representative local practice is spot/band placement 3–5 cm from the seed at ~5 cm depth to avoid seed burn. Rate logic: approx. 125 kg/ha DAP supplies ~22.5 kg N/ha and ~25.1 kg P/ha (conversion: P2O5 to P factor 0.4364; 0.46×0.4364=0.2007; 125×0.2007≈25.1). No K applied, consistent with common practice in this zone. N amount here contributes to the exact 90 kg N/ha scenario requirement.

Early topdress at ~knee-high stage using calcium ammonium nitrate (CAN, ~26% N). Broadcast by hand and timed to coincide with rainfall; not incorporated (surface). Representative event for Kitale smallholder practice. Rate logic: ≈130 kg/ha CAN provides ~33.8 kg N/ha. N amount chosen to help reach the exact 90 kg N/ha total while maintaining typical timing and source.

Second topdress with CAN, broadcast before rain, aligning with common split-N practice to reduce loss risk and sustain growth through rapid vegetative development. Rate logic: ≈129.6 kg/ha CAN supplies ~33.7 kg N/ha. This split plus the basal DAP yields exactly 90.0 kg N/ha in total. No P or K added at topdress, consistent with local practice.
